newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot power prices end flat to lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot power prices end flat to lower.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. finished Wednesday flat to lower against Tuesday's levels ahead of the expected shutdown of the Ginna nuclear power plant, market sources said.
The 470 megawatt (MW) Ginna 1 station in Ontario, N.Y., will begin to be idled late Wednesday to perform diagnostic tests on its transformer, the operator Rochester Gas and Electric Corp said.
The outage generally helped support spot power values in the New York Power Pool (NYPP) district despite modest power demand in the state, marketers said.
In western NYPP, peak, non-firm electricity for Thursday delivery was assessed at $20.00-$23.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), flat from Tuesday.
Western NYPP power for non-firm delivery during Thursday's light load hours was discussed at $14.00-$15.00, compared with Tuesday's range of $14.00-$14.75.
In the eastern part of NYPP, peak, non-firm electricity for next-day delivery was pegged near $26.00, down from a quote of $30.00-$32.00 amid today's decline crude oil and natural gas prices.
Off-peak, non-firm electricity for next-day delivery in eastern NYPP was still valued in the $14.50-$15.00 range.

In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), next-day, peak electricity for Thursday at the Northeast Utilities border was discussed at $31.00-$33.00, sharply narrower than Tuesday's assessement at $30.00-$37.00.

The scheduled startup of the 510 MW Vermont Yankee nuclear station in Vernon, Vt., Thursday would ease a recent generating tightness in the pool and transmission limits to move power from New York to New England.
"Mainly it's because of a problem with the New York state transmission system power East," said a Northeast trader, referring to the primary factor for high prices in NEPOOL.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for next-day delivery to the NU border was quoted at $19.00-$20.00, down from Tuesday's range of $21.00-$22.00.
